title: Field Orientation
objectives: Explain why ecologists use quadrats to sample a habitat
Lay out a quadrat and identify every organism inside it
Record counts accurately for later analysis

sequence.instruction: Talk to Ranger Okafor outside the field station.
sequence.hint: Follow the yellow arrow and the compass at the top of the screen.
npcLines: Welcome to the reserve! I'm Ranger Okafor. We think the disturbed lot next door is losing plant diversity, and we need data to prove it.
We measure biodiversity with quadrats: square frames we lay on the ground. We count every organism inside, then compare habitats.
Grab a quadrat kit from the table by the station, and I'll show you on the practice plot.

sequence.instruction: Pick up a quadrat kit from the table by the field station.
sequence.hint: It's the white frame and clipboard on the wooden table.

feedback.correct: Quadrat kit collected: a 2 m × 2 m frame, a field guide and a tally sheet.

sequence.instruction: Walk to the practice plot (marked P) and lay out your quadrat.
sequence.hint: Stand next to the orange flag marked Plot P and press E (or tap the button).

feedback.correct: Quadrat placed. Only count what's inside the frame.

sequence.instruction: Count every organism in the practice quadrat. Choose a species from the field guide, then tap each one you see.
sequence.hint: Compare shapes and colors with the field guide swatches. Every plant must be tallied before the plot is complete.

feedback.correct: Practice plot recorded. Nice careful counting!

sequence.instruction: Tell Ranger Okafor what you found on the practice plot.
npcLines: Great work! See how every species in the frame now has a count? That's your raw data.
Next, run the full Habitat Biodiversity Survey: two quadrats each in the meadow, the forest and the disturbed lot. Then we'll see which habitat is most diverse.
